questions.question: What are the advantages and limitations of free hand sectioning?
questions.solution_html:
• Freehand sectioning is a technique commonly used to prepare thin sections of plant tissue for
  • microscopic examination. The method consists of firmly holding a piece of fresh or preserved
  • material between the left hand thumb and forefinger and cutting with a sharp razor.
  • Advantages
  • ➢ Quick and cost-effective.
  • ➢ Can be done almost anywhere, making it ideal for fieldwork or classroom demonstrations.
  • ➢ Suitable for fresh and soft tissues.
  • ➢ Limitations
  • ➢ Less precise compared to microtome sectioning.
  • ➢ Uniformity and thickness of sections can vary.
  • ➢ Not ideal for very hard or tiny specimens.
  • (Give marks for any other relevant points)

questions.question: Briefly describe Agarose gel electrophoresis
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly describe Agarose gel electrophoresis.
  • ➢ Agarose gel electrophoresis is a laboratory technique to separate, identify, and analyze DNA
  • RNA based on their size and charge in a porous agarose gel matrix.
  • ➢ It is also used for the separation of proteins
  • ➢ The movement of charged molecules in an electric field.
  • ➢ DNA and RNA are negatively charged due to their phosphate backbone, so they migrate
  • towards the positive electrode (anode) when an electric field is applied.
  • ➢ Molecules are separated by size—smaller fragments move faster and travel farther through
  • the gel, while larger fragments move slower.

questions.question: What is DNA barcode? What is its significance in species identification?
questions.solution_html:
• DNA barcoding is a technique to identify and authenticate species in biological samples by
  • analysing small, standardised DNA fragments known as DNA barcodes.
  • 2 | Pa ge
  • Significance
  • ➢ DNA barcoding allows for the quick identification of species, even from small or degraded
  • samples.
  • ➢ DNA barcoding identifies species based on genetic differences, making it more accurate and
  • independent of external factors.
  • ➢ DNA barcoding can reveal cryptic species that look similar but are genetically distinct.
  • ➢ Conservation of biodiversity by identifying and monitoring endangered or endemic species.
  • ➢ Used in wildlife crime investigations to identify poached animals or smuggled plant
  • products.
